key_insight: The paper shows that modeling railway pricing as a relational multi-agent problem with graph structure helps agents learn competitive dynamics under partial observability.
engineering_relevance: For liberalised rail markets, the approach offers a practical way to improve dynamic pricing policies while respecting privacy and anti-collusion constraints.
method: Build an entity graph of operational units to encode competition, coordination, and connectivity.
Use a multi-agent TD3 variant with multi-layer relational graph convolution to learn entity representations.
Aggregate relational signals with a learned attention mechanism before pricing decisions.
evidence_signal: In a rail pricing reinforcement learning environment, the method outperformed relational and non-relational baselines in two market settings with increasing complexity, improving both revenue and stability.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of the constructed market graph and the realism of the simulator relative to real railway operations.
paper_title: Relational Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Dynamic Pricing in High-Speed Railway Markets
